mainTopic: Lashes for eating sacred food improperly, and which steps are required for בכורים (הנחה, קריאה, תנופה)
overview: The גמרא finishes discussing רבא's count of lashes for a זר who ate an עולה. It explains that כל שבקודש פסול does not add lashes, because an עולה was never fit to eat. It agrees that רבי אליעזר's כליל תהיה rule does add lashes; רבא was only counting from his own verse. Next, רב גידל quotes רב that a כהן who eats a חטאת or אשם before זריקה gets lashes, since a לאו הבא מכלל עשה counts as a full לאו. רבא disproves this from the kosher-animal verses, so the teaching is restated: a זר who eats before זריקה is exempt, because the ban on a זר applies only once the כהנים may eat. The גמרא then turns to בכורים: without הנחה they are invalid, but without קריאה they are still valid. Using רבי זירא's rule, this holds only while קריאה is still possible. Seeming contradictions in רבי יוחנן's words are solved by tying each statement to a different תנא. This leads to the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב over where waving of בכורים is learned. A new teaching of רבי יצחק about בכורים begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not also lashes for eating disqualified sacred food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge: the eater should also get lashes under רבי אליעזר's rule that any disqualified sacred food carries a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything sacred that became disqualified, the Torah gave a prohibition against eating it! So he should get lashes for that too.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a question that began just before. The גמרא asks why the person who ate the עולה does not get one more set of lashes under the rule of כל שבקודש פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא listed several sets of lashes for a זר who ate an עולה. The challenge points to another prohibition he seems to break: רבי אליעזר's rule that eating any disqualified sacred food is a לא תעשה. If that rule applies here, the count of lashes is missing one.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything sacred that became disqualified
A negative commandment; breaking it can bring lashes
Eating it

phrases.english: Anything sacred that is disqualified –

phrases.aramaic: בָּא הַכָּתוּב לִיתֵּן לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ!
phrases.english: the verse comes to place a prohibition on eating it!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁבַּקֹּדֶשׁ פָּסוּל בָּא הַכָּתוּב לִיתֵּן לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge to רבא's count of lashes, which comes before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's count of lashes for eating an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The count leaves out the prohibition of כל שבקודש פסול, which should add another set of lashes.

steps.title: The rule only covers food that was once fit to eat
steps.stepSummary: כל שבקודש פסול applies only to sacred food that was fit to eat before it became disqualified. Here the food was never fit to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies only where the food was fit before it became disqualified. Here, even before it became disqualified, it was not fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The rule of כל שבקודש פסול does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is about food that was allowed to be eaten and then became unfit. An עולה is never eaten at all, so nothing "changed" from fit to unfit. Without that change, this extra prohibition is never triggered.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies only...
Before it became disqualified
Fit, suitable (here: fit to be eaten)

steps.whatToRemember: כל שבקודש פסול only covers sacred food that went from fit to unfit, not food that was never fit to be eaten.

phrases.english: This applies only where
before its disqualification it was fit;
here, before its disqualification,
it was also not fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּקוֹדֶם פְּסוּלוֹ חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every disqualified sacred food carries the prohibition, including an עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only food that was fit to eat before it was disqualified carries the prohibition, so an עולה is not included.

steps.title: Why not lashes under רבי אליעזר's כליל תהיה rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the eater does not also get lashes under רבי אליעזר's other rule: anything that is כליל (burned entirely) may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him also get lashes under the other teaching of רבי אליעזר. It was taught: רבי אליעזר says, anything that falls under 'it shall be burned entirely' has a prohibition against eating it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to the count of lashes. רבי אליעזר has another rule, and an עולה seems to fit it exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely on the מזבח, so it is כליל. רבי אליעזר learns from the פסוק that anything כליל carries a לא תעשה against eating it. So eating an עולה should add one more set of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall be burned entirely (completely on the מזבח)
And let him be flogged
The other one

phrases.english: But let him also be flogged
according to the other teaching of Rabbi Eliezer.
As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Anything that falls under 'It shall be burned entirely' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:16

phrases.english: the verse comes to place a prohibition on eating it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 2 answered the first challenge, a second challenge is raised from another rule of רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עולה is כליל, and רבי אליעזר gives a לא תעשה for eating anything כליל, so another set of lashes is missing from the count.

steps.title: Yes, he does get those lashes; רבא only counted from his own verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the eater gets lashes for כליל too. רבא was only counting the lashes that come from the verse he was discussing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. רבא was only speaking from this verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. It explains that רבא's list was never meant to include every possible set of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not rejected, it is accepted: the כליל prohibition does add lashes. רבא's count was limited to the lashes learned from the verse he was working with. So his number was not a full total of all lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (an agreement with the question)
Verse
He was saying

steps.confusionAlert: אין הכי נמי does not reject the question. It agrees with it and then explains why there was no real contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: A count of lashes given by an אמורא may be limited to one source, not a full total.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
and Rava was speaking from this verse.
phrases.notes: He means רבא only counted the lashes that come from the verse he was discussing, not from every source.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי וְרָבָא מֵהַאי קְרָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by agreeing with it
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreeing with the challenge and limiting what the original statement meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's count was a full total, so leaving out כליל is a mistake.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כליל lashes do apply. רבא counted only from one specific verse.

steps.title: A כהן who eats a חטאת or אשם before the sprinkling gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: a כהן who eats from a חטאת or אשם before its blood is sprinkled gets lashes. A memory sign is given first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב (memory sign: כוזא): A כהן who ate from a חטאת or an אשם before the sprinkling of the blood gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling of רב. A כהן who eats these offerings too early gets lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may eat a חטאת or אשם, but only after the blood is sprinkled on the מזבח. רב says that eating it before then is not just wrong, it is a sin that brings lashes. The source for this is given in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign to help remember a list of teachings
Sin-offering
Guilt-offering
Sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח
He gets lashes

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
(A memory sign: kaf, vav, zayin, alef)
phrases.notes: These letters help you remember the statements of רב that follow. כ hints to כהן and ז hints to זר.

phrases.english: A priest who ate from a sin-offering or a guilt-offering
before the sprinkling – is flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about lashes for eating offerings too early
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who eats a חטאת or אשם before זריקה gets lashes.

steps.title: רב's source: a prohibition that comes from a positive command
steps.stepSummary: The verse says the כהנים eat offerings 'with which atonement was made,' so they may eat only after atonement. רב holds that a לאו הבא מכלל עשה counts as a full לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The verse says, 'And they shall eat them, with which atonement was made.' After atonement, yes; before atonement, no. And a prohibition that comes from a positive command counts as a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב gives lashes and explains his source. It also states the key idea behind his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse only says, in a positive way, when the כהנים eat: after atonement. From that we learn that eating before atonement is forbidden. This is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, and רב treats it like a real לאו, which brings lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Atonement (here: done through the sprinkling of the blood)
A prohibition learned by implication from a positive command
A positive commandment

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a לאו הבא מכלל עשה brings lashes is the real issue here. רבא challenges exactly this idea in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: Usually a לאו הבא מכלל עשה is treated like an עשה, and an עשה brings no lashes. רב is taking the stricter view that it counts as a real לאו.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says:
'And they shall eat them, with which atonement was made,'
phrases.notes: שמות 29:33

phrases.english: after atonement – yes,
before atonement – no.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה, – לָאו הוּא.
phrases.english: A prohibition that comes from a positive command – is a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and verse behind רב's ruling in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does a כהן get lashes for eating before זריקה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse allows eating only after כפרה. The prohibition that comes from this positive command counts as a full לאו.

steps.title: רבא's challenge from the kosher-animal verses
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues: 'that you may eat' already implies other animals are forbidden. If such an implied prohibition were a full לאו, the Torah would not need to say 'this you shall not eat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: 'And every animal that splits the hoof, has the hoof cloven in two, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may eat.' 'That you may eat' means no other animal may you eat. If it is as you say, why do I need the verse 'This you shall not eat'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב's idea that a לאו הבא מכלל עשה is a full לאו. He uses the verses about kosher animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From 'that you may eat' we already know, by implication, that other animals are forbidden. If that implied prohibition were already a full לאו, the next verse's clear לאו would add nothing. So the extra verse suggests that an implied prohibition is not a full לאו, and that would mean no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Splits the hoof (a sign of a kosher animal)
Chews the cud (a sign of a kosher animal)
Why do I need it? (suggests a verse would be extra)

phrases.english: Rava raises an objection:
'And every animal that splits the hoof
and has the hoof cloven in two
and chews the cud among the animals
that you may eat,'
phrases.notes: דברים 14:6

phrases.english: 'That you may eat' –
but no other animal may you eat.
And if it is as you say,
why do I need 'This you shall not eat'?
phrases.notes: דברים 14:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the idea in step 6 that a לאו הבא מכלל עשה is a full לאו
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's idea that a לאו הבא מכלל עשה is a full לאו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an implied prohibition were already a full לאו, the clear לאו 'this you shall not eat' would be extra. So the implied prohibition must have the weaker level of an עשה.

steps.title: The corrected version of רב's teaching
steps.stepSummary: After רבא's challenge, the גמרא gives a different version of רב's statement. A זר who eats from a חטאת or אשם before זריקה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if רב said anything, this is what he said: a non-כהן who ate from a חטאת or an אשם before the blood was sprinkled is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier version of רב's statement, the one about a כהן getting lashes, and gives a new one. In the new version, a זר who eats before זריקה is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא showed that an implied prohibition, a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, does not bring lashes, so the old version could not stand. The new version changes both the person (a זר instead of a כהן) and the result (exempt instead of lashes). The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said. This phrase brings a corrected version of an earlier statement.
A non-כהן
Sprinkling the offering's blood on the altar
Exempt, here meaning no lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the earlier version. Before, the case was a כהן who gets lashes. Now it is a זר who is exempt.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, this is how it was stated:
phrases.notes: The earlier version, about a כהן getting lashes, is being dropped because of רבא's question.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
A non-priest who ate from a sin-offering or a guilt-offering
before the sprinkling of the blood is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 7 by giving a different version of רב's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the original teaching in a different form
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב said a כהן who eats before זריקה gets lashes because of an implied prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב actually said that a זר who eats before זריקה is exempt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זר who eats from a חטאת or אשם before זריקה is exempt.

steps.title: Why the זר is exempt before זריקה
steps.stepSummary: The verse puts 'they shall eat them, with which atonement was made' right next to 'a זר shall not eat.' So the ban on a זר only applies when the כהנים are allowed to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The verse says, 'And they shall eat them, with which atonement was made,' and then, 'a זר shall not eat.' Wherever the first part applies, meaning the כהנים may eat, the ban on a זר applies too. Wherever the first part does not apply, the ban on a זר does not apply either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the זר is exempt. It answers from the פסוק, which ties the ban on a זר to meat that the כהנים are allowed to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before זריקה, even כהנים may not eat the meat, so the words 'and they shall eat them' do not apply yet. Because the two halves of the verse go together, the words 'a זר shall not eat' do not apply yet either. So there is no לאו for the זר, and he gets no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
We read it about this, meaning the verse applies to this case
Atonement was made with them, which happens through זריקה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common way of learning a פסוק: when two parts of one verse sit together, one part only applies where the other part applies.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says:
"And they shall eat them, with which atonement was made"
phrases.notes: שמות 29:33. The same verse goes on to say that a זר may not eat.

phrases.english: Wherever we can read about it
"and they shall eat them, with which atonement was made,"
we read about it "and a non-priest shall not eat holy food."
And wherever we cannot read about it
"and they shall eat them, with which atonement was made,"
phrases.notes: Before זריקה there is no atonement yet, so the כהנים can't eat either.

phrases.english: we do not read about it "and a non-priest shall not eat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on a זר is tied to the time when the כהנים may eat. Before זריקה that time has not come, so the ban does not apply yet.

steps.title: For בכורים, placing is required but reciting is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי הושעיה, says that בכורים are not valid without הנחה by the altar, but they are still valid without קריאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי הושעיה: with בכורים, placing them by the altar holds back their validity, but reciting the verses does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about בכורים. It brings a ruling on which steps must be done for the fruit to be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעכב means a step is so necessary that without it the whole thing is not valid. Here the הנחה is that kind of step. The קריאה is a מצוה, but skipping it does not ruin the בכורים, so the כהן may still eat them.

keyTerms.meaning: The first fruits, brought to the בית המקדש
Placing the fruit by the altar
Reciting the verses said over בכורים
Holds back. Without this step the בכורים are not valid.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Hoshaya said:
With first fruits, placing them by the altar is required for them to be valid,
but reciting the verses is not required for them to be valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unconnected to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without הנחה the בכורים are not valid. Without קריאה they are still valid.

steps.title: His other ruling: בכורים kept past the holiday must rot
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר also said that בכורים kept until after סוכות must be left to rot. That seems to be because the verses can no longer be recited, which would mean קריאה is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי אלעזר really say that? He also said, in the name of רבי הושעיה: if someone set aside בכורים before the holiday and the holiday passed, they must rot. Isn't that because he can no longer recite the verses over them? And if reciting is not required, why must they rot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר with another ruling of his own. The two rulings seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses may only be recited until סוכות. If the fruit must rot after סוכות, it seems that missing the קריאה makes the בכורים invalid. That clashes with step 10, which said the קריאה is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say that? This phrase opens a contradiction.
The holiday, meaning סוכות
They must be left to rot
If you think that

phrases.english: Did Rabbi Elazar really say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: But Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Hoshaya said:
If one set aside first fruits before the holiday,
and the holiday passed while he still had them, they must be left to rot.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מָצֵי לְמִיקְרֵי עֲלֵיהֶן?
phrases.english: Isn't that because he can no longer recite the verses over them?
phrases.notes: After סוכות it is too late to say the verses over בכורים.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ קְרִיָּיה אֵין מְעַכֶּבֶת בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: And if you think that reciting is not required for them to be valid,
why must they be left to rot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10 with another statement by the same sage.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that קריאה is not required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His ruling that the fruit must rot after סוכות only makes sense if missing the קריאה makes the בכורים invalid.

steps.title: Answer from רבי זירא's rule about בילה
steps.stepSummary: Using רבי זירא's rule: if a step can still be done, leaving it out does not make the offering invalid. If it can no longer be done, the offering is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר follows רבי זירא, who said: anything that is fit for mixing, the mixing does not hold it back. Anything that is not fit for mixing, the mixing does hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction using a rule of רבי זירא about mixing a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before סוכות the קריאה can still be done, so skipping it does not make the בכורים invalid, as step 10 said. After סוכות it can no longer be done at all, so now its absence makes the fruit invalid, and that is why it must rot. What matters is being able to do the step, not actually doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with רבי זירא's rule
Mixing the flour and oil of a מנחה
Fit for mixing, meaning it is possible to mix it

steps.whatToRemember: A step that is not required is only skipped safely while it is still possible to do it. Once it can no longer be done at all, its absence makes the item invalid.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא's rule is about whether the mixing CAN be done, not whether it actually WAS done.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי זירא's rule is a well-known principle that appears in other places as well.

phrases.english: It is like the view of Rabbi Zeira.
For Rabbi Zeira said:
Anything that is fit for mixing,
phrases.notes: He means the flour and oil of a מנחה, when it is possible to mix them.

phrases.english: the mixing does not hold back its validity;
and anything that is not fit for mixing,
the mixing does hold back its validity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a general principle that separates the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fruit must rot after סוכות because קריאה is always required.
steps.terutzMaskana: קריאה is only required once it can no longer be done, which is after סוכות.

steps.title: A different source for the rule about first fruits
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר יעקב teaches the בכורים rule in the name of רבי יוחנן, and so he has to deal with a clash between two statements of רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר יעקב teaches this rule as something רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן. Because of that, he faces a problem: one statement of רבי יוחנן seems to go against another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It says the rule from Step 10 is really רבי יוחנן's, and warns that this will create a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10 the rule was quoted from רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי הושעיה. Now רבי אחא בר יעקב puts it in רבי יוחנן's mouth. Once רבי יוחנן owns it, it has to match everything else רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: it is difficult for him
one statement of רבי יוחנן against another of his

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מַתְנֵי לַהּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov teaches it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule about בכורים from Step 10.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan,
and it is difficult for him:
Rabbi Yochanan against Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מַתְנֵי לַהּ כִּדְרַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the statement discussed in Steps 10-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that הנחה is required and קריאה is not is רבי יוחנן's statement.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's answer to רבי אסי seems to clash
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן told רבי אסי that בכורים which can't have קריאה become permitted once they reach the בית המקדש, with no mention of הנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say that for בכורים, missing הנחה makes them invalid and missing קריאה does not? But רבי אסי asked him: from when are בכורים permitted to the כהנים? He answered: fruits that can have קריאה, from when he recites over them. Fruits that cannot have קריאה, from when they enter the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new version by quoting another statement of רבי יוחנן that seems to say something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his answer to רבי אסי, fruits that can't have קריאה are still permitted, so missing קריאה does not ruin them even when it is impossible. But the first statement, read with רבי זירא's rule from step 12, means that once קריאה is impossible, its absence does make them invalid. He also never mentions הנחה, which suggests it is not required. That clashes with 'הנחה is required.'

keyTerms.meaning: holds back, makes the מצוה invalid if left out
from when?
fit to have the verses recited over them
the inside of the בית המקדש (literally 'the face of the House')

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate clashes are hiding here, one about קריאה and one about הנחה. The answer to רבי אסי never says 'הנחה is not needed.' The problem comes from what he leaves out.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say
that for first fruits, placement is required for them,
but recitation is not required for them?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But Rabbi Asi asked Rabbi Yochanan:
First fruits, from when are they permitted to the priests?
And he said to him:
Those fit for recitation: from when he recites over them.
And those not fit for recitation:
from when they have entered the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the contradiction that Step 13 warned about.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that הנחה is required and קריאה is not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His answer to רבי אסי lets בכורים that can't have קריאה be eaten, and it skips הנחה entirely.

steps.title: Two contradictions stated clearly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names both problems: recitation against recitation, and placement against placement.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty between the two statements on קריאה, and a difficulty between the two statements on הנחה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the challenge as two separate contradictions inside רבי יוחנן's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On קריאה, one statement ('קריאה is not required', read with רבי זירא's rule) treats impossible קריאה as invalidating, while the other permits fruits that can't have קריאה. On הנחה, one statement requires it and the other ignores it.

keyTerms.meaning: one statement about recitation against the other
one statement about placement against the other

phrases.english: Recitation against recitation is difficult,
and placement against placement is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the challenge of Step 14 into two clear points.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יוחנן's two statements.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each statement says the opposite of the other on both קריאה and הנחה.

steps.title: Each statement follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: On קריאה, one statement follows רבי שמעון and one follows רבנן. On הנחה, one follows רבי יהודה and one follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Recitation against recitation is not difficult: this one follows רבי שמעון, that one follows רבנן. Placement against placement is also not difficult: this one follows רבי יהודה, that one follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן is not contradicting himself. He is reporting the views of different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view that impossible קריאה invalidates (the fruits must rot) matches רבי שמעון. The view that such fruits are still permitted matches רבנן. Saying הנחה is not needed matches רבי יהודה, and saying הנחה is required matches רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult
this one ... that one (each follows a different opinion)
the Sages, the majority view

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions go away because each statement follows a different תנא: רבי שמעון or רבנן on קריאה, and רבי יהודה or רבנן on הנחה.

phrases.english: Recitation against recitation is not difficult:
this follows Rabbi Shimon, that follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון is the view that the fruits must rot when קריאה is no longer possible.

phrases.english: Placement against placement is also not difficult:
this follows Rabbi Yehuda, and that follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה is the view that does not require הנחה; רבנן require it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both contradictions raised in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each statement follows a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements are רבי יוחנן's own view, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן is reporting different תנאים: רבי שמעון or רבנן on קריאה, and רבי יהודה or רבנן on הנחה.

steps.title: Where is רבי יהודה's view found?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יהודה's view about הנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the view of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks where we see that רבי יהודה does not require הנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 tied one statement to רבי יהודה without showing where his view comes from. The גמרא now asks for that source.

keyTerms.meaning: what is?

phrases.english: What is the view of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind part of the answer in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing רבי יהודה's view on הנחה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads 'and you shall place it' as waving
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה reads 'וְהִנַּחְתּוֹ' as תנופה (waving), because placement is already written in 'וְהִנִּיחוֹ.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, 'and you shall place it' means waving. Do you say it means waving, or maybe it means actual placing? When the verse already says 'and he shall place it,' placing has been mentioned. So how do I explain 'and you shall place it'? It means waving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא that shows how רבי יהודה reads the verses about הנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two verses that sound like placing: 'וְהִנִּיחוֹ' (the כהן places it) and 'וְהִנַּחְתּוֹ' (you place it). רבי יהודה says the first already covers placing, so the second must mean waving. This is the source Step 16 tied to his view that missing הנחה does not make the בכורים invalid. The ברייתא gives the reading of the verses but does not spell out why this leads to that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and you shall place it' (דברים 26:10)
waving the offering
'and he shall place it' (דברים 26:4)
so how do I explain this verse?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה reads 'וְהִנַּחְתּוֹ' as תנופה, so only 'וְהִנִּיחוֹ' speaks about placing. רבנן read both as placing.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
'And you shall place it': this is waving.
phrases.notes: דברים 26:10

phrases.english: You say this is waving,
or maybe it is only actual placing?
When it says 'and he shall place it',
phrases.notes: דברים 26:4

phrases.english: placing has already been stated.
So how do I explain 'and you shall place it'?
This is waving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה reads 'וְהִנַּחְתּוֹ' as תנופה, since placing is already written in 'וְהִנִּיחוֹ'.

steps.title: Who argues with רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא disagrees with רבי יהודה's reading of 'והנחתו' as waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who disagrees with רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just showed where רבי יהודה's view comes from. Now it asks who holds the other side. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 the גמרא said one statement follows רבי יהודה and one follows רבנן. Now it wants a named source for the רבנן side. That would show who reads 'והנחתו' as real placing and not as waving.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period
Who disagrees

phrases.english: And who is the tanna who disagrees
phrases.notes: He means the תנא behind the רבנן side from step 16.

phrases.english: with Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding רבי יהודה's source, the גמרא looks for the opposing תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The name and source of the תנא who disagrees with רבי יהודה about הנחה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns waving from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: The opposing תנא is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He learns תנופה from 'ולקח הכהן הטנא מידך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. A ברייתא teaches that 'And the כהן shall take the basket from your hand' shows that בכורים need waving. These are the words of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי אליעזר בן יעקב as the one who argues with רבי יהודה. It brings a ברייתא where he learns waving from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree that בכורים need waving. They argue about where we learn it. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב gets waving from 'מידך', so 'והנחתו' stays free to mean actual placing. That is why he holds placing matters.

keyTerms.meaning: The basket the בכורים are brought in
Require

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב does not argue about whether בכורים need waving. He agrees they do. He just learns it from a different פסוק, and that leaves 'והנחתו' meaning placing.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
as it is taught: "And the priest shall take the basket from your hand"
phrases.notes: דברים 26:4

phrases.english: this taught about first fruits
that they require waving,
the statement of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who learns תנופה from 'ולקח הכהן הטנא מידך'. That leaves 'והנחתו' meaning placing.

steps.title: Why does this verse teach waving?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר בן יעקב sees waving in 'ולקח הכהן הטנא מידך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how this פסוק shows waving. The words only say the כהן takes the basket. This question sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says nothing openly about waving. So the גמרא needs to show how רבי אליעזר בן יעקב finds waving inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason / source?

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How 'ולקח הכהן הטנא מידך' teaches תנופה.

steps.title: The 'hand' comparison to peace-offerings
steps.stepSummary: A גזרה שוה of 'יד' links בכורים to שלמים. Both the כהן and the owner wave together: the כהן's hands go under the owner's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'hand' and 'hand' in שלמים. Here it is written, 'And the כהן shall take the basket from your hand.' There it is written, 'His hands shall bring the fire-offerings of ה׳.' Just as here a כהן is involved, so too there a כהן is involved. Just as there the owner is involved, so too here the owner is involved. How does that work? The כהן places his hands under the owner's hands and waves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source. The word 'hand' appears both by בכורים and by שלמים, and שלמים are waved. So בכורים are waved too, by the כהן and the owner together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison works in both directions. From בכורים we learn that a כהן is part of the waving of שלמים. From שלמים we learn that the owner is part of the waving of בכורים. To fit both, the כהן puts his hands under the owner's hands and they wave together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned (here through a גזרה שוה, a link between two פסוקים that share a word)
Peace-offerings, which are waved
The owner who brings the offering
How does that work? (used to fit two rules together)
Waves

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns waving of בכורים through 'יד–יד' from שלמים. The כהן and the owner wave together, with the כהן's hands underneath. Because his source for waving is different, 'והנחתו' stays as real placing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the רבנן side of step 16 can treat הנחה as a real requirement. Their source for waving does not use up the word 'והנחתו'.

phrases.english: It is derived from "hand" "hand" from peace-offerings:
It is written here: "And the priest shall take the basket from your hand,"
and it is written: "His hands shall bring the fire-offerings of God,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:30, about שלמים. The same פסוק goes on to talk about waving.

phrases.english: just as here, a priest —
phrases.notes: 'Here' means בכורים and 'there' means שלמים.

phrases.english: so too there, a priest;
just as there, the owner —
so too here, the owner.
How so?
The priest places his hands
beneath the hands of the owner and waves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by giving the גזרה שוה behind רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה of 'יד' from שלמים teaches waving for בכורים. It is done jointly, with the כהן's hands beneath the owner's.

steps.title: A new statement about first fruits begins
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר אדא, quoting רבי יצחק, begins a new statement about בכורים. It continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: בכורים...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new statement about בכורים. Only the first word appears here, and the rest continues right after. This is a setup for the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new teaching. It is not part of the רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב discussion, which just ended. What it says about בכורים comes in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rava bar Adda says that Rabbi Yitzchak says:
First fruits,
